mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has climbed from -39.1 to -14.0 in three weeks, and transit reopening re-enables non-essential trips with a short lag, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose 25.1 points from t-3w (-39.1) to t-0w (-14.0)
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is at or below the last-28-day mean of -25.45 even as TRANSIT continues to rise toward baseline.

mechanism_narrative: The reopening impulse has stalled: RETAIL_REC slipped from -16.7 to -17.9 and PARKS dropped 4.4 points at t-0w, showing discretionary outings have peaked, so RETAIL_REC drifts lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 4 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 16.3 at t-1w to 11.9 at t-0w while RETAIL_REC fell from -16.7 to -17.9
failure_condition: After PARKS falls more than 4 points week-on-week, the following two-week RETAIL_REC mean lands above -17.9.

mechanism_narrative: Households stay home-anchored (RESIDENTIAL +2.6, WORKPLACES -29.0) while grocery spending stays above baseline (+6.9), so consumption remains concentrated in essential channels and RETAIL_REC fails to recover over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays above 0 while WORKPLACES stays below -25
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is 2.6 and GROCERY_PHARM is 6.9 at t-0w while WORKPLACES is -29.0
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds -25.45 while RESIDENTIAL remains above 0 and GROCERY_PHARM remains above 0.

mechanism_narrative: Each week-on-week TRANSIT gain above 4 points re-enables non-essential travel and pulls RETAIL_REC up within seven days, so the next week's RETAIL_REC mean exceeds -17.9.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises more than 4 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 4.9 points from t-1w (-18.9) to t-0w (-14.0)
failure_condition: A week with a TRANSIT gain above 4 points is not followed within one week by a RETAIL_REC level above -17.9.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has declined from 3.3 to 2.6, indicating stay-at-home rules are being relaxed; each point of decline releases out-of-home trips and lifts RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 3.3 at t-3w to 2.6 at t-0w while TRANSIT rose 25.1 points
failure_condition: Two consecutive weeks with RESIDENTIAL below 3.0 are followed by a two-week RETAIL_REC mean at or below -17.9.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS at +11.9 above baseline marks the spring outdoor season, and outdoor trip generation spills into adjacent retail-and-recreation venues, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS is +11.9 above baseline at t-0w and has been positive since t-1w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is at or below the last-28-day mean of -25.45 while PARKS remains above 0.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery demand is rolling over (7.4 to 6.9) while transit keeps climbing (-18.9 to -14.0), so trip purposes are broadening beyond essentials and RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises while GROCERY_PHARM falls in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell 0.5 points while TRANSIT rose 4.9 points at t-0w
failure_condition: Weeks in which TRANSIT rises and GROCERY_PHARM falls are followed by a two-week RETAIL_REC mean below -17.9.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES has flatlined near -29 for two weeks, so daytime office footfall is not returning and weekday retail demand stalls, leaving RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-on-week change stays between -1 and +1 point for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved only from -29.3 at t-1w to -29.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds -25.45 while WORKPLACES remains within one point of -29.
